newsitem.title: GREECE: Greece slaps 15 pct retroactive tax on derivatives.
newsitem.headline: Greece slaps 15 pct retroactive tax on derivatives.

text.p: Greece's finance ministry has slapped a 15 percent retroactive tax on income from derivatives earned by residents and some classes of entrepreneurs effective January 8, according to a ministry circular.
The tax will affect all contracts initiated in the past that expire or may be unwound from January 8.

"Therefore for income from deals or contracts on financial derivatives, irrespective of their contract date, earned by individuals and entrepreneurs that do not keep records of third class accounting books of the KVS, there is a withholding tax of 15 percent at expiration or upon an agreed income payment prior to that date from January 8," the circular said.
Individual companies, general or limited partnerships are among those that are not required to keep third class accounting books. Therefore, they are subject to taxation.
"The above...do not apply to income earned by entrepreneurs that keep records of third class accounting books of the KVS or investment companies or mutual funds," it said.
National Economy Minister Yannos Papandoniou has said that the government was against retroactive taxation because it upset the business climate without bringing in much revenues.

Greece imposed a 7.5 percent tax on interest earned from government securities effective January 1, 1997. Papandoniou had pre-announced it in November. --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
